newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Merrill Lynch to help Romania raise credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to help Romania raise credit rating.

text.p: Merrill Lynch, which guided Romania's return to the international capital market this year, will help the country upgrade its credit rating and grant further assistance in issuing Eurobonds, an executive said.

"Clearly we support the efforts of the National Bank of Romania (central bank) in securing a credit upgrade by the rating agencies," Paul Raphael, managing director of the securities company's emerging markets unit, told Reuters on Friday.
Central bank sources said the BNR was aiming for a BBB rating which defines obligations for which there is currently a low expectation on risk investment.

Earlier this year, Romania was awarded a BB-plus score, by the Japan Credit Rating agency, somewhat higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standards and Poors and IBCA and the BA- three from Moody's Investors Service.

"We believe that in 1997 there is going to be a chance for Romania to establish a track record for the second year in a raw in terms of effective macro-economic management," Raphael said. "If they can do it in 1997, I think a rating will certainly be a distinct possibility."
This year, Merrill Lynch helped Romania rejoin the world capital market after more than a decade of isolation imposed by the ousted commumist regime of late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
It handled two medium-term issues on capital markets for the BNR -- a $50 million private placement last November and $225 million worth of three-year Eurobonds in June.
Raphael praised the BNR for its "critical role in leading the way in an extremely professional manner" in the process.

Raphael also said the market had "received very favourably" Emil Constantinescu's victory over ex-Communist Ion Iliescu in this week's presidential election. Parliamentary polls had been won two weeks earlier by centrists who back the new president.

"I think it is a very positive environment for (Romania's) Eurobonds. They have reached 360 and they are now 300. This is the first time in recent history when there was a smooth handover of one governemnt to another and the markets are taking it very well," Raphael said.
In 1991, rioting miners opposed to reforms sacked offices in Bucharest, prompting Iliescu to remove Prime Minister Petre Roman. The leftist government which followed slowed reforms.
Raphael said Merrill Lynch would help Bucharest authorities raise up to $200 million through a private placement and autumn municipal bonds to upgrade infrastructure.

The company would also assist the electricity authority Renel RA and state bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA go on the Euro-markets with "the first true Eurobonds by non-sovereign issuers" by early 1997, he said.

"I thing it's too early to discuss specifics about the issue we have. One has to determine the maturity, the amount, the pricing as close as possible to the end," Raphael said. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
